subject: Money
title: The Decoy Effect
description: A quick win: understand The Decoy Effect.

hook.text: Small popcorn $3. Large $7. Nobody buys large. Add medium for $6.50 and suddenly large looks smart.

buildup.text: The medium isn't meant to sell. It's a decoy that makes the expensive option look like a bargain.

discovery.text: The Economist offered print-only for $59, web for $125, and both for $125. The print decoy boosted combos.

twist.text: Without the decoy, 68% chose web-only. With it, 84% chose the combo. One useless option changed everything.

climax.text: Decoys are everywhere: subscription tiers, airline seats, car trims. The middle option is often the trap.

punchline.text: The option you ignore chose for you.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a decoy option?
options: To sell at a lower price
To make another option look better
